proof_findings.reason: Every stated possible state has positive physical probability. Stock trading is restricted to time zero and maturity; observed intermediate stock marks are not tradable quotes. Deterministic bank reinvestment/borrowing permits the terminal-equivalent treatment of dated payments. A pricing probability is not identified with a physical frequency.

For the compact calibrated simplex, the null direction preserving mass and stock mean reduces a linear optimizer to at most two states. The convex splitting argument also decomposes any law into these basic laws. Repeated outcomes and singleton support at the forward are handled. With the forward strictly inside the stock range, each possible state appears positively in a feasible basic law, so their average is strictly positive.

The affine superhedge envelope is coercive because min(x)<F<max(x); its minimum occurs at a breakpoint or a flat segment adjoining one. Active slopes bracket zero, producing a feasible one/two-state pricing law that attains the hedge cost. Negating the payoff supplies the subhedge. At a nonreplicable endpoint the nonnegative hedge residual is positive in a possible state, giving arbitrage; mixing positive laws obtains every strict interior price. A singleton range implies affine replication.

The weighted cross-variation second-moment bound follows from conditional independence and zero conditional means. Coefficient freezing uses the isometry and localization; drift terms vanish by finite variation/Cauchy-Schwarz, and the Taylor remainder is controlled on compact sets. The proof is explicitly restricted to continuous adapted coefficients and C1,2 functions, with stopped coefficients handled by dominated convergence at the single stopping discontinuity. No general semimartingale formula is assumed.

The orthogonal Brownian exposure, minimum instantaneous-variance stock position and residual variance are derived by completing a square. An extra traded instrument matches two instantaneous exposures only under the stated nonzero determinant. Financing, terminal matching, admissibility and global existence are not inferred from this local linear system.

proof_findings.topic: Remaining risk premium and martingale scope
proof_findings.reason: The constant exponential-normal tilt changes the second Brownian driver alone; finite-dimensional independent increments preserve the first driver and the joint Brownian structure. Equivalent finite-horizon laws preserve the stochastic-integral limit in probability. For the explicit bounded volatility, stopped Ito and the integral inequality bound E[S_t^2] by S0^2 exp(.25^2 t); the resulting finite integral second moment makes stock a true L2 martingale. Different digital expectations exclude common admissible replication. A normalized density is correctly not claimed to prove a stock martingale for arbitrary unbounded coefficients.

The mixed derivative coefficient and factor drift under the selected pricing law are correct. The chapter labels this a candidate equation and requires regularity, terminal matching and a suitable discounted martingale for a valuation representation; it does not silently assert existence, uniqueness or a general stochastic-premium theorem.

Applying the continuous formula between finitely many deterministic event dates and telescoping supplies the exact jump increments. The integral Taylor remainder uses the pre-jump derivative and remains valid for both signs of jump within the domain. Post-jump rebalancing cannot earn the preceding stock move. This proof is not presented as a random-time compensator or Levy-process theorem.

For the same law and nonnegative call payoff, nested observations shrink survival pathwise. The result is not applied to nonnested observations or changed dynamics. Equal terminal distributions need not identify barriers or averages, and extra Asian fixings have no universal monotone effect. Additional intermediate stock trading requires conditional calibration, which the original finite model deliberately does not impose.

Default is processed before a coincident coupon; elapsed premium is paid at default, protection at the separately specified settlement date. Recovery and the seller paid fraction enter protection only. Each amount is discounted at its payment date before terminal accumulation. The joint-state model does not replace joint expectations with products of marginal averages, and is not described as a current legal CDS convention or bilateral CVA model.

Strictly positive state annuities make every basic-law denominator positive. A mixture ratio is a convex average of basic-law ratios weighted by their annuities; nonconstant endpoints are excluded for strictly positive pricing laws by the endpoint hedge argument applied to loss minus spread times annuity. The zero-annuity counterexample explains why discarding zero denominators can conceal an unbounded spread.

Conditional orthogonality yields E[(sum H_i DeltaW1_i DeltaW2_i)^2] <= ||H||infinity^2 t mesh. The vector formula for xy supplies drift rho and square-integrable stochastic terms, hence E[X_t Y_t]=rho t.

Independently integrated the tilted density; at T=4 the digital prices are .5 and .158655253931457 for lambda zero and one half. The limitation for unbounded volatility is explicit.

For f(S)=S^3/10000, delta is 3 and gamma is .06 at S=100. Exact residuals for jumps -20 and +50 are 11.2 and 87.5; the constant-gamma terms 12 and 75 omit the cubic remainder. The finite-event telescoping and pre-event holding requirement answer the proof and timing parts.

At barrier 120 the monitored payoff is (0,10,0,0), with prices 50/13 and 25/26; terminal-only monitoring gives (0,10,10,0), priced 125/26 under both laws. Audited the pathwise nested-event proof and both directions of the extra-fixing Asian counterexample.

The independent date-interval accrual automaton gives immediate-settlement protection PV 279250/10403, net value 51629775/2299063 and spread 740571/4033790. Restoring delayed settlement and full Decline seller performance adds 125/17 protection PV and 405717/8067580 annual spread. Dependence and discount timing explain why marginal averages cannot replace the ledger.

The annuity-weighted convex-combination proof is valid with positive denominators; nonconstant positive-law ranges are open. With L=(1,0), A=(0,1), p/(1-p) diverges as p tends to one, so the zero denominator cannot be silently removed.

Both positive laws calibrate the original stock and bank, so a physical law does not become uniquely identified by no-arbitrage. At the uniquely identified year-one Spike mark 140, the conditional terminal-stock PV is 1275/13, not 140. Making that mark tradable changes the market and invalidates the retained laws.

All six claims are corrected with defensible scope: terminal calibration versus histories, exposure rank, local instrument matching versus global admissibility, exact jump gaps, pricing versus physical default intensities, and sampling precision versus contract definition. The three proposed identification/contract/implementation tests are concrete and their limitations explicit; the 12-point rubric does not demand a unique open-response opinion.

The answered teaching example distinguishes nonunique pricing laws from computational accuracy and disputed payment dates. Retention answers are the replication singleton, residual variance 4 dt, jump gap 9, knockout at barrier equality, and .04 per year = 400 basis points.
